# Invoices Dashboard Apps Script failures — what is wrong and the fix

**Task:** rec0QCIMVezkpaKZR · 26 Aug 2026 · Prepare-only, nothing changed yet

## Summary

Your Invoices Dashboard script (the one that copies "3: to pay" invoice emails into Airtable) keeps running out of its daily Gmail allowance. It runs every 30 minutes, and most evenings the allowance is gone by about 5pm, so every run after that fails until Google resets the limit early next morning. Google has sent 12 failure summary emails since 30 July. The fix is one setting change: run the script every 2 hours instead of every 30 minutes.

## What is failing (evidence from the failure emails)

- 12 failure summaries from n***@***.com between 30 Jul and 25 Aug 2026, all for script "Invoices Dashboard", function `syncGmailToAirtable`, time-based trigger.
- The run times in every email are :07 and :37 past the hour, which confirms the trigger still fires every 30 minutes. That is 48 runs a day.
- The dominant error, in every email, is: "Exception: Service invoked too many times for one day: premium gmail." Examples: 9 failed runs on 29 Jul (5:07pm to 9:07pm), 4 on 21 Aug, 8 on 24 Aug. Failures always start late afternoon and repeat every half hour, which is exactly what a used-up daily allowance looks like.
- Minor extras: one Airtable "Bandwidth quota exceeded" on the Invoices table (22 Aug, 7:07pm) and three one-off Google server errors on 24 Aug. These are side effects of running so often, not separate problems.

## Why (the shared root cause)

Google gives your account ONE daily pot of Gmail calls, shared by every Apps Script you own. Three scripts are drinking from it: Invoices Dashboard, Meetings Intake and Meetings to Supabase (the two sibling tasks in this run show the same "premium gmail" error). Between them the pot empties by late afternoon, then all three fail until the reset. Slowing one script helps all three; slowing all three fixes it.

A fix plan for this exact problem was prepared on 25 Aug (task recsyCXB30AqD0bg8) but that task was Cancelled, so nothing was ever changed.

## Impact

Evenings only: new invoice emails are not copied into the Invoices tab until the next morning's successful run. Nothing is corrupted and nothing is wrongly marked paid; the sync only creates records. This is a delay, not a data problem.

## Fix plan — recommended option

**Change the trigger from every 30 minutes to every 2 hours.** One setting in the Apps Script Triggers screen, no code change, two minutes of work. It cuts this script's runs from 48 to 12 a day (a 75% cut in its Gmail draw) and also relieves the Airtable bandwidth blip. The dashboard's manual sync button still exists for anything urgent, and invoices do not need 30-minute freshness.

Pair it with the sibling fixes for the two Meetings scripts so the shared pot actually lasts the day. Then watch for one week: success is zero "premium gmail" failure emails for 7 days.

Options considered and set aside:
- 60-minute trigger only: a half measure; with three scripts sharing one pot it may still run dry.
- Rewriting the script to use fewer Gmail calls: worth doing later, but a code change with test risk, not needed to stop the failures.
- Moving the sync off Apps Script into daily-ops: biggest change, only justified if the trigger fix fails.

**Carrying this out will involve:** The Invoices Dashboard trigger is changed from every 30 minutes to every 2 hours in the Apps Script Triggers screen (your Google account, no code change), one manual sync is run to catch anything missed, and failure emails are watched for 7 days to confirm zero quota errors.

# Task: rec0xxPRaE3LP2yAH — Meetings Intake Apps Script failing

**Status:** PREPARED. Diagnosis confirmed via live test. Awaiting Kevin's approval.

---

## What is actually broken

The deployed "Meetings Intake" Apps Script (project id `1FJlPDhB-xNwrCbIk1IiAjTA3FI3-CAHMDCr3pOZnrQLQUpUs28PtyAe9`) is running every 15 minutes as a time trigger. When the Gmail daily quota is exhausted, `GmailApp.getUserLabelByName()` on line 172 throws the exception:

> `Exception: Service invoked too many times for one day: premium gmail.`

This was confirmed live by calling `?action=count` on the deployed web app URL — it returned that exact error right now. The `syncMeetings()` function has no try/catch wrapper around its Gmail calls (lines 229 and 236), so this exception propagates uncaught. Google's trigger runner logs it as a failure and sends a failure summary email.

The deployed web app health check (`no action` query) responds correctly with `{"status":"ok","message":"Gmail Meetings Intake v1"}`, which confirms the Script Properties and the deployment itself are intact.

---

## Why is the quota being exhausted now?

The PR #6 fix (June 2026) already dropped the trigger from every-5-min to every-15-min to fix exactly this issue. Something has increased Gmail API usage since then:

**Most likely cause:** The Supabase twin (`gmail-meetings-supabase-script.gs`) was added to the repo on 21 July 2026 and, if deployed as a separate Apps Script project with its own 15-min trigger on the same Gmail account, doubles the Gmail API calls. 96 runs/day x 2 scripts = 192 trigger runs, each calling `GmailApp.getUserLabelByName()` and potentially `GmailApp.getUserLabels()`. This matches the timing of failures starting around 21 August (a month after the Supabase script was available to deploy).

The inbound triage agent (launched 24 August) also runs Gmail reads, but failures started on 21 August so it is not the trigger.

---

## What needs to be fixed

Two separate things, in priority order:

### Fix 1 (code fix — stops Google sending failure emails immediately):

Add a try/catch around the Gmail calls in `syncMeetings()` so a quota exception is caught and logged rather than thrown. This makes the script fail gracefully and silently instead of generating a failure email on every quota-exceeded run.

In `/Users/kevinbrittain/Projects/leadership-dashboard/gmail-meetings-script.gs`, replace the two lines at the top of `syncMeetings()` that call Gmail:

```
  var label = findLabel();
  if (!label) {
    var e2 = { error: 'Gmail label "' + LABEL_NAME + '" not found', created: 0 };
    Logger.log('RESULT: ' + JSON.stringify(e2));
    return e2;
  }

  var threads = label.getThreads(0, 25);
```

With:

```
  var label, threads;
  try {
    label = findLabel();
    if (!label) {
      var e2 = { error: 'Gmail label "' + LABEL_NAME + '" not found', created: 0 };
      Logger.log('RESULT: ' + JSON.stringify(e2));
      return e2;
    }
    threads = label.getThreads(0, 25);
  } catch (gmailErr) {
    var quota = { skipped: 'gmail_quota', error: String(gmailErr) };
    Logger.log('RESULT: ' + JSON.stringify(quota));
    return quota;   // exit cleanly — no failure summary generated
  }
```

This is the same pattern as the `doGet` wrapper, applied to the time-trigger path.

### Fix 2 (root cause — reduces Gmail API usage):

Check whether the "Meetings to Supabase" Apps Script project has a 15-min time trigger running against the same Gmail account (`kevin@runpreneur.org.uk`). If it does, **disable or delete that trigger**. The Airtable intake is still the live system of record. The Supabase version should not have an active trigger until the Meetings module migrates.

To check: go to `script.google.com` → open the "Meetings to Supabase" project → Triggers (clock icon). If there is a `syncMeetings` trigger set to every 15 minutes, delete it.

---

The trigger runs at "Head" (the saved code), so the fix is live as soon as the code is saved in the Apps Script editor. The versioned `/exec` deployment also needs a bump so the Fix button on the Tasks tab picks up the change:

2. Apply the code change above (use `monaco.editor.getModels()[0].setValue(text)` with the updated source fetched from the raw GitHub URL — do not use cmd+v, it corrupts UTF-8 characters)

- All Airtable field IDs in the script are valid: Meetings table `tblNodbh9B3WLzCIK`, Tasks `tblqB8b22hKBL4PF1`, Team `tblco0p2OnlLQVAX7` all respond 200 with correct data

- The code change is isolated to the Gmail catch path and does not affect any other logic

# Cloudflare KV daily write limit — investigation result and fix plan

## Summary
The culprit is neither Fantasy Football Meta nor the eBay engine. It is the OD **sms-email-bridge** Worker. It writes a "last poll time" note to KV storage every single minute, 24 hours a day. That is 1,440 writes per day against a free limit of 1,000. The limit is guaranteed to trip at around 16:40 UTC every day, which is why the alerts keep repeating. Recommended fix: a one-line code change, cost £0. No upgrade needed.

## Evidence (from Cloudflare's own usage stats, read-only)
Daily KV writes per store, 23 to 26 Aug:

| Store (Worker) | 23 Aug | 24 Aug | 25 Aug | 26 Aug (to 12:05) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SMS_STATE (sms-email-bridge) | 1,440 | 1,439 | 1,440 | 688 |
| PREDICTIONS (Fantasy Football) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 3 |
| STATS (Fantasy Football) | 5 | 2 | 1 | 3 |
| GMAIL_AUTH (drive-upload) | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

Fantasy Football writes 2 to 5 times a day. The eBay Arbitrage Engine does not use Cloudflare KV at all; it is a local Python tool on the Mac (checked the whole repo, zero KV code). The task description's assumption about those two Workers was wrong.

## The exact cause
`workers/sms-email-bridge/worker.js`, line 110. The Worker polls GoHighLevel for new inbound SMS every minute (cron `* * * * *`), and the first thing each poll does is:

`await env.SMS_STATE.put('lastPollTime', new Date().toISOString());`

One write per minute, whether or not any SMS arrived. The only thing this value feeds is the Worker's own `/test` diagnostic page. Nothing else in the codebase reads it. The two useful writes (last message timestamp, forwarded count) only fire when an SMS actually arrives, which is rare.

## Hidden damage you should know about
The write sits BEFORE the error handling. Once the daily limit trips (about 16:40 UTC), the write fails, the whole poll crashes, and **inbound SMS stops being forwarded to your email from roughly 17:40 to 01:00 UK time, every day**. This has likely been happening for at least the last four days.

## Options

**Option A (recommended): fix the code. £0.**
Remove the every-minute heartbeat write, or throttle it to once an hour. After the fix the whole account uses under 50 KV writes a day against the 1,000 limit, leaving huge headroom. Delivered through the normal /fix build pipeline: edit, test, deploy with wrangler, verify live. Also restores the evening SMS forwarding outage as a side effect.

**Option B: upgrade to Workers Paid. $5/month (about £4).**
Makes the symptom go away but pays monthly for a heartbeat nobody reads, and hides the design flaw. Not recommended while Option A is a one-line change.

## Recommendation
Option A. Approve and a /fix task edits `workers/sms-email-bridge/worker.js` (remove or hourly-throttle the line 110 write), redeploys the Worker, and verifies the write count drops in the same usage stats used above. No money committed, no plan change.

**Carrying this out will involve:** A code-fix task is queued: one line changed in the sms-email-bridge Worker to stop the every-minute KV write, then redeploy and verify writes drop below 50/day. No Cloudflare upgrade, no spend. The daily limit alerts and the evening SMS-forwarding outage both stop.

# Meetings to Supabase — Apps Script failures: findings and fix plan

## What is failing
The Google Apps Script "Meetings to Supabase" (function `syncMeetings`, 15-minute time trigger, account kevin@runpreneur.org.uk). It is the Supabase shadow twin of the Meetings Intake script: it reads Gmail label "15: meeting summary" and writes meetings and tasks to Supabase. Source: `gmail-meetings-supabase-script.gs` in the leadership-dashboard repo.

## The evidenced error
I read all four failure emails in label 12. Every single failure, across every email, is the same one line:

`Exception: Service invoked too many times for one day: premium gmail.`

- 19 Aug email: 21 failures (18 Aug 22:12 to 19 Aug 04:27 PST)
- 21 Aug email: 25 failures (21 Aug 02:12 to 04:12, then 20:12 to 22 Aug 02:12 PST)
- 22 Aug email: 9 failures (02:27 to 04:27 PST)
- 25 Aug email: 15 failures (24 Aug 23:57 to 25 Aug 04:27 PST)

There is no Supabase or connection error anywhere in the four emails. The Supabase write path is not the problem.

## Cause
The Gmail service inside Apps Script has a daily call quota shared across EVERY script on the account. "premium gmail" is Google naming the paid Workspace tier of that quota. Once the account's daily allowance is used up, this script dies on its first Gmail call each run until the quota window resets. The failure blocks end at almost exactly 04:27 PST every day, which is the reset point; the rest of the day the script runs clean.

This script's own Gmail draw is small (a handful of calls per run when the label is empty). It is a victim of the shared quota, not the main consumer. The same quota exhaustion is behind the Meetings Intake and Invoices Dashboard failures covered by the sibling tasks this run; the heavy-consumer question belongs to those investigations.

## Impact
No meetings are lost. A failed run leaves the trigger label in place, so any meeting summary arriving during the outage window syncs on the first clean run after reset. The damage is a delay of up to several hours overnight, plus daily failure-email noise into label 12.

One design note worth knowing: both meeting scripts strip the same trigger label after processing. Whichever runs first on a thread removes it, so the other side relies on its own dedupe and processed-label guards. This has not caused the current failures but is worth revisiting at Supabase cutover.

## Fix plan — recommended option
Change this script's time trigger from every 15 minutes to every 1 hour.

- One click in the Apps Script console (Triggers, edit, Minutes timer to Hour timer). No code change, no redeploy, fully reversible.
- Cuts this script's Gmail draw by roughly 75 percent and cuts its failure-email noise by the same.
- Hourly is plenty for a shadow build: Airtable remains system of record and the Airtable twin keeps its own cadence.

Alternatives considered and not recommended now: (a) wrapping the first Gmail call to swallow quota errors quietly — hides the signal without reducing the draw; (b) merging the two meeting scripts into one dual-write script — the right long-term shape, but a code change during migration for a problem the trigger change resolves.

The real cure for the account-wide exhaustion sits with whichever script is burning the bulk of the quota; that is the sibling tasks' territory. This change fixes what this script controls.

**Carrying this out will involve:** Kevin (or an approved agent session) opening the Meetings to Supabase project in the Apps Script console and switching the syncMeetings trigger from every 15 minutes to hourly. No code or deployment changes. Overnight failure emails for this script should drop sharply from the next quota window.
